Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# eureka

`eureka` is a command-line tool that lets you quickly record an idea using your preferred editor and have that idea stored in a git-backed ideas repository.

Think of it as a very quick way to capture short notes: run the command, write your idea, and it will be saved to your ideas repository so you can revisit it later.

![demo](assets/demo.gif)

## Usage

Run the command with no arguments to capture a new idea. The first time you run it you will be asked to configure the path to your ideas repository.

View stored ideas with the view flag:

```sh
$ eureka --view
```

### Flags

```sh
    --clear-config    Clear your stored configuration
-v, --view            View ideas with your $PAGER environment variable (falls back to less)
```

### Recommended alias

An easy-to-remember alias is `idea`:

**Zsh**

```sh
echo 'alias idea="eureka"' >> ~/.zshrc
```

**Bash**

```sh
echo 'alias idea="eureka"' >> ~/.bashrc
```

**Fish**

```sh
echo 'alias idea="eureka"' >> ~/.config/fish/config.fish
```

## Notes

This README has been sanitized to keep only user-facing information about what the program does and how to use it. Internal implementation details (build instructions, CI badges, package manifests, tests, and developer documentation) have been removed.

use log::LevelFilter;
use std::error::Error;
use std::fmt::{Display, Formatter};

use crate::Directive;
use crate::FilterOp;

#[derive(Default, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct ParseResult {
    pub(crate) directives: Vec<Directive>,
    pub(crate) filter: Option<FilterOp>,
    pub(crate) errors: Vec<String>,
}

impl ParseResult {
    fn add_directive(&mut self, directive: Directive) {
        self.directives.push(directive);
    }

    fn set_filter(&mut self, filter: FilterOp) {
        self.filter = Some(filter);
    }

    fn add_error(&mut self, message: String) {
        self.errors.push(message);
    }

    pub(crate) fn ok(self) -> Result<(Vec<Directive>, Option<FilterOp>), ParseError> {
        let Self {
            directives,
            filter,
            errors,
        } = self;
        if let Some(error) = errors.into_iter().next() {
            Err(ParseError { details: error })
        } else {
            Ok((directives, filter))
        }
    }
}

/// Error during logger directive parsing process.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct ParseError {
    details: String,
}

impl Display for ParseError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "error parsing logger filter: {}", self.details)
    }
}

impl Error for ParseError {}

/// Parse a logging specification string (e.g: `crate1,crate2::mod3,crate3::x=error/foo`)
/// and return a vector with log directives.
pub(crate) fn parse_spec(spec: &str) -> ParseResult {
    let mut result = ParseResult::default();

    let mut parts = spec.split('/');
    let mods = parts.next();
    let filter = parts.next();
    if parts.next().is_some() {
        result.add_error(format!("invalid logging spec '{spec}' (too many '/'s)"));
        return result;
    }
    if let Some(m) = mods {
        for s in m.split(',').map(|ss| ss.trim()) {
            if s.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            let mut parts = s.split('=');
            let (log_level, name) =
                match (parts.next(), parts.next().map(|s| s.trim()), parts.next()) {
                    (Some(part0), None, None) => {
                        // if the single argument is a log-level string or number,
                        // treat that as a global fallback
                        match part0.parse() {
                            Ok(num) => (num, None),
                            Err(_) => (LevelFilter::max(), Some(part0)),
                        }
                    }
                    (Some(part0), Some(""), None) => (LevelFilter::max(), Some(part0)),
                    (Some(part0), Some(part1), None) => {
                        if let Ok(num) = part1.parse() {
                            (num, Some(part0))
                        } else {
                            result.add_error(format!("invalid logging spec '{part1}'"));
                            continue;
                        }
                    }
                    _ => {
                        result.add_error(format!("invalid logging spec '{s}'"));
                        continue;
                    }
                };

            result.add_directive(Directive {
                name: name.map(|s| s.to_owned()),
                level: log_level,
            });
        }
    }

    if let Some(filter) = filter {
        match FilterOp::new(filter) {
            Ok(filter_op) => result.set_filter(filter_op),
            Err(err) => result.add_error(format!("invalid regex filter - {err}")),
        }
    }

    result
}

import os, pty, sys, time, select
env = dict(os.environ)
args = sys.argv[1:]
i = args.index("--")
for kv in args[:i]:
    if kv.startswith("-u"):
        env.pop(kv[2:], None)
    else:
        k, v = kv.split("=", 1)
        env[k] = v
cmd = args[i+1:]
pid, fd = pty.fork()
if pid == 0:
    os.execve(cmd[0], cmd, env)
else:
    def read_for(secs):
        out = b""
        end = time.time() + secs
        while time.time() < end:
            r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.1)
            if r:
                try:
                    d = os.read(fd, 4096)
                    if not d: break
                    out += d
                except OSError:
                    break
        return out
    print("BEFORE INPUT:", repr(read_for(1.0)))
    os.write(fd, b"/tmp/repo1\n")
    print("AFTER INPUT:", repr(read_for(1.0)))
    try:
        os.kill(pid, 9)
    except Exception: pass
    os.waitpid(pid, 0)
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the `eureka` binary and place it at ./executable.
#
# The build is fully offline: every crate comes from the local cargo registry
# cache. TLS (https://) and SSH remotes are supported when the system provides
# OpenSSL and libssh2 development files; otherwise those transports are left
# out and only local/git:// remotes work.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")"

export PATH="/usr/local/cargo/bin:${HOME}/.cargo/bin:${PATH}"
export CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true

if ! command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "error: cargo is required to build eureka" >&2
    exit 1
fi

features=()
have_pkg() { command -v pkg-config >/dev/null 2>&1 && pkg-config --exists "$1"; }

if have_pkg openssl || have_pkg libssl; then
    features+=("https")
fi
if have_pkg libssh2; then
    features+=("ssh")
fi

feature_flag=()
if [ "${#features[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    feature_flag=(--features "$(IFS=,; echo "${features[*]}")")
fi

build() {
    cargo build --release --offline --locked "$@"
}

if ! build "${feature_flag[@]}"; then
    if [ "${#features[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
        echo "warning: building without optional network transports" >&2
        build
    else
        exit 1
    fi
fi

cp target/release/eureka ./executable
chmod +x ./executable
echo "built ./executable"
EOF
chmod +x compile.sh; rm -f executable 2>/dev/null; ls -la executable 2>&1 | head -2"}

# cache. TLS (https://) and SSH remotes are supported when the system provides
# OpenSSL and libssh2 development files; otherwise those transports are left
# out and only local/git:// remotes work.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")"

export PATH="/usr/local/cargo/bin:${HOME}/.cargo/bin:${PATH}"
export CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true

if ! command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "error: cargo is required to build eureka" >&2
    exit 1
fi

features=()
have_pkg() { command -v pkg-config >/dev/null 2>&1 && pkg-config --exists "$1"; }

if have_pkg openssl || have_pkg libssl; then
    features+=("https")
fi
if have_pkg libssh2; then
    features+=("ssh")
fi

feature_flag=()
if [ "${#features[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    feature_flag=(--features "$(IFS=,; echo "${features[*]}")")
fi

build() {
    cargo build --release --offline --locked "$@"
}

if ! build "${feature_flag[@]}"; then
    if [ "${#features[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
        echo "warning: building without optional network transports" >&2
        build
    else
        exit 1
    fi
fi

cp target/release/eureka ./executable
chmod +x ./executable
echo "built ./executable"
EOF
chmod +x compile.sh; rm -f executable 2>/dev/null; ls -la executable 2>&1 | head -2

//! Git operations backed by libgit2: switch to the ideas branch, stage the
//! README, commit and push.

use std::path::Path;

use git2::{
    BranchType, Cred, CredentialType, ErrorClass, ErrorCode, ObjectType, PushOptions,
    RemoteCallbacks, Repository,
};

pub const BRANCH: &str = "main";
pub const REMOTE: &str = "origin";
pub const IDEAS_FILE: &str = "README.md";

/// Newer libgit2 releases reworded the "repository not found" message
/// ("at" instead of "from"). Keep the wording stable across library versions.
pub fn normalize_error(e: git2::Error) -> git2::Error {
    const CURRENT: &str = "could not find repository at ";
    const STABLE: &str = "could not find repository from ";

    if e.class() == ErrorClass::Repository {
        if let Some(rest) = e.message().strip_prefix(CURRENT) {
            return git2::Error::new(e.code(), e.class(), format!("{}{}", STABLE, rest));
        }
    }
    e
}

fn malformed_url(url: &str) -> git2::Error {
    git2::Error::new(
        ErrorCode::InvalidSpec,
        ErrorClass::Net,
        format!("malformed URL '{}'", url),
    )
}

fn unknown_scheme(url: &str) -> git2::Error {
    git2::Error::new(
        ErrorCode::InvalidSpec,
        ErrorClass::Net,
        format!("unknown scheme for URL '{}'", url),
    )
}

/// Reject URLs whose explicit port is out of range before handing them to
/// libgit2, mirroring the strict URL validation of older releases.
fn validate_remote_url(url: &str) -> Result<(), git2::Error> {
    let Some(idx) = url.find("://") else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    let scheme = &url[..idx];
    if scheme.eq_ignore_ascii_case("file") {
        // Local transport: the URL is used as a path and never parsed.
        return Ok(());
    }
    if url.chars().any(char::is_whitespace) {
        return Err(malformed_url(url));
    }
    let rest = &url[idx + 3..];
    let authority = rest.split('/').next().unwrap_or("");
    if authority.matches('@').count() > 1 {
        return Err(malformed_url(url));
    }
    let host_port = match authority.rfind('@') {
        Some(at) => &authority[at + 1..],
        None => authority,
    };
    if host_port.contains('%') {
        return Err(malformed_url(url));
    }
    let port = if host_port.starts_with('[') {
        match host_port.find(']') {
            Some(end) => host_port[end + 1..].strip_prefix(':'),
            None => None,
        }
    } else {
        host_port.rsplit_once(':').map(|(_, p)| p)
    };
    if let Some(port) = port {
        if !port.is_empty() && port.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) {
            match port.parse::<u32>() {
                Ok(n) if n <= 0xffff => {}
                _ => return Err(malformed_url(url)),
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Translate URL parsing failures of the bundled libgit2 into the wording
/// used by earlier releases.
fn normalize_url_error(url: &str, e: git2::Error) -> git2::Error {
    if e.class() == ErrorClass::Invalid {
        match e.message() {
            "invalid argument: 'port'" => return unknown_scheme(url),
            "invalid argument: 'host'" | "invalid argument: 'url->host'" => {
                return malformed_url(url)
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    if e.class() == ErrorClass::Net && e.message() == "invalid url: malformed hostname" {
        return malformed_url(url);
    }
    e
}

pub struct Git {
    repo: Repository,
}

impl Git {
    pub fn open<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> Result<Self, git2::Error> {
        Ok(Git {
            repo: Repository::open(path)?,
        })
    }

    /// Make sure the ideas branch exists (creating it from `HEAD` if needed),
    /// check it out and point `HEAD` at it.
    pub fn checkout_branch(&self) -> Result<(), git2::Error> {
        let branch = match self.repo.find_branch(BRANCH, BranchType::Local) {
            Ok(branch) => branch,
            Err(_) => {
                let head = self.repo.head()?;
                let commit = head.peel_to_commit()?;
                self.repo.branch(BRANCH, &commit, false)?
            }
        };

        let target = branch.get().peel(ObjectType::Commit)?;
        self.repo.checkout_tree(&target, None)?;
        self.repo.set_head(&format!("refs/heads/{}", BRANCH))?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Stage the ideas file.
    pub fn add(&self) -> Result<(), git2::Error> {
        let mut index = self.repo.index()?;
        index.add_path(Path::new(IDEAS_FILE))?;
        index.write()?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Commit whatever is staged on top of `HEAD` with the given message.
    pub fn commit(&self, message: &str) -> Result<(), git2::Error> {
        let mut index = self.repo.index()?;
        let tree_id = index.write_tree()?;
        let tree = self.repo.find_tree(tree_id)?;
        let signature = self.repo.signature()?;
        let parent = self.repo.head()?.peel_to_commit()?;
        self.repo.commit(
            Some("HEAD"),
            &signature,
            &signature,
            message,
            &tree,
            &[&parent],
        )?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Push the ideas branch to the `origin` remote.
    pub fn push(&self) -> Result<(), git2::Error> {
        let mut remote = self.repo.find_remote(REMOTE)?;

        let config = self.repo.config()?;
        let mut callbacks = RemoteCallbacks::new();
        callbacks.credentials(move |url, username_from_url, allowed| {
            if allowed.contains(CredentialType::SSH_KEY) {
                return Cred::ssh_key_from_agent(username_from_url.unwrap_or("git"));
            }
            if allowed.contains(CredentialType::USER_PASS_PLAINTEXT) {
                return Cred::credential_helper(&config, url, username_from_url);
            }
            Cred::default()
        });

        let mut options = PushOptions::new();
        options.remote_callbacks(callbacks);

        // Pushing goes to the push URL when one is configured.
        let url: Option<String> = match remote.pushurl() {
            Ok(Some(push_url)) => Some(push_url.to_owned()),
            _ => remote.url().ok().map(str::to_owned),
        };
        if let Some(url) = &url {
            validate_remote_url(url)?;
        }

        let refspec = format!("refs/heads/{0}:refs/heads/{0}", BRANCH);
        match remote.push(&[refspec.as_str()], Some(&mut options)) {
            Ok(()) => Ok(()),
            Err(e) => Err(match url {
                Some(url) => normalize_url_error(&url, e),
                None => e,
            }),
        }
    }
}
